description: RFC 8620 §5.2 says 'If supplied, the value MUST be a positive integer greater than 0'. The handlers in email.rs:118, mailbox.rs:93, thread.rs:83, submission.rs:104, identity.rs:81 parse maxChanges via v.as_u64() which accepts 0 as a valid u64, then pass it to get_changes. The MemoryBackend treats max_changes=Some(0) as a limit of 0 entries (per the limit.saturating_add(1) sentinel pattern), so the backend returns has_more=true and no changes — silently wrong behavior for a client that sends maxChanges:0 by mistake. Should return invalidArguments instead. Trigger: POST {method:"Email/changes", args:{accountId:"x", sinceState:"0", maxChanges:0}} → currently returns hasMoreChanges:true, created:[], not an error.
title: maxChanges=0 is silently accepted; RFC requires rejection
